summary: WSL2 DoH stub + Hyper-V vEthernet causes asymmetric routing and breaks access to internal k8s API over VPN
description: Multiple engineers reported inability to reach internal Kubernetes API (kube-apiserver) from developer laptops when connected to Corporate VPN. Problem correlates with Windows machines running WSL2 and a DoH/DoT stub resolver (system or third-party), which create a Hyper-V vEthernet adapter and local UDP/TCP endpoints. Traffic to cluster control-plane IPs appears to be routed out the wrong interface causing TCP resets and TLS handshake failures.
impact: Developers cannot kubectl to production-like clusters while on VPN; CI jobs run from local machines fail. Affects ~8 reported engineers across us-west office and remote contractors. Productivity loss estimated at 6-8 engineer-hours so far.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On Windows 11 machine with WSL2 enabled and DoH client running (either built-in Windows DoH or a user-level DoH client), connect to Redwood Corporate VPN (WireGuard).
2) Confirm new vEthernet (WSL) interface present in 'ipconfig /all'.
3) Attempt 'kubectl get pods' against internal cluster (cluster IPs routed via VPN).
4) Observe long timeouts or TLS handshake errors.
5) Disable WSL2 or stop DoH client and retest; connectivity is restored.
observed_behavior: kubectl timeouts, TLS handshake errors 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' in some captures, connection resets (RST) seen in tcpdump on client. Traceroute shows traffic goes out local vEthernet (Hyper-V) interface intermittently rather than the VPN interface.
expected_behavior: All traffic destined for internal cluster CIDRs should be routed via VPN interface; DNS lookups should resolve internal service names to VPN-provided DNS servers or be bypassed as configured by split-tunnel policy.
logs:
Mar 10 09:12:21 client-tcpdump: SYN to 10.12.5.3 from 192.168.50.18 sent on vEthernet (WSL) - no SYN-ACK
Mar 10 09:12:21 vpn-daemon: route add 10.12.0.0/16 -> wg0
Windows Event: NetworkProfile change: vEthernet (WSL) registered with metric 25, interface index 14
kubectl: dial tcp 10.12.5.3:6443: connect: connection refused (after retries)
WireGuard status: interface up, AllowedIPs includes 10.12.0.0/16
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: WSL2 creates a virtual interface with a more-preferred metric, Windows route selection prefers local vEthernet for specific destination address ranges when DoH client binds to 127.0.0.53 style addresses or exposes a local DNS proxy.
Reproduced on two machines: one with built-in Windows DNS-over-HTTPS (win11 feature) and one with third-party DoH client (cloudflared). Both show same symptom when WSL2 active.
Packet captures on client show SYN leaving on vEthernet and never reaching VPN peer; tcpdump on VPN gateway shows no inbound SYN from that client IP when failure occurs.
Workaround test: setting Interface Metric for vEthernet to a higher value (less preferred) restores correct routing to VPN interface and fixes kubectl connectivity.

Potential root cause: interaction between Windows DNS/DoH stub resolving and WSL2's NAT/virtual adapter triggering Windows to choose local adapter for certain IPv4 destinations. Split-tunnel or policy-based routes installed by VPN may not have strong enough precedence due to interface metrics.
Related config: some users have persistent static routes added by dev tools that overlap VPN CIDRs (need to check 'route print -4').
comments: Lena Park (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Initial report from eng on-call. Provided client tcpdump and Windows 'route print' output. Symptoms started after Windows update and WSL2 kernel patch.
Diego Martinez (assignee) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed on my test VM. Reproduced with cloudflared and with system DoH. Prioritized because it blocks deployments.
SRE (Amit Rao) - 2026-03-11: Captured traffic at edge for affected client; no packets from client observed when failure occurs. Suggest check of interface metrics and persistent routes on Windows.

Platform Eng (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-11: Noted that WireGuard adds policy routes but Windows may honor interface metrics over route specificity in some cases; asked for 'netsh interface ipv4 show interfaces' output.

Diego Martinez - 2026-03-12: Applied temporary mitigation guidance to affected users (increase vEthernet metric or stop DoH client). Requesting a more permanent client-side policy or onboarding change.
Lena Park - 2026-03-12: Customers/devs confirmed workaround works; documenting steps for internal KB.
mitigation_steps:
Temporary: On affected Windows machines run as admin:
  netsh interface ipv4 set interface "vEthernet (WSL)" metric=400
  or stop the DoH client/service (e.g., cloudflared) and restart VPN client.
Alternative: Add explicit persistent route that forces VPN interface for 10.12.0.0/16: route add 10.12.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0 <wg_gateway> metric 1 -p

Longer-term: Push a configuration update to the Corporate VPN client to set stronger policy routes (use 'route metric 1' and enforce via WireGuard pre/post-up scripts) and publish recommended interface-metric settings in onboarding docs.
Investigate adding a startup hook for Windows VPN provisioning that sets vEthernet interface metric to reduce precedence when WSL2 is present.
next_steps: 1) SRE to prototype WireGuard pre/post-up script to enforce route metrics and test in staging. 2) Defect: Add client policy to onboarding docs and VPN installer to set recommended metrics. 3) Follow up with Windows team to track any Windows DoH change that alters adapter selection behavior.
